day: Our Lady of Sorrows on Tuesday of week 24 in Ordinary Time
text:
At the foot of the cross, where Jesus is dying, his gaze falls not on his own pain but on the people he loves. He makes sure his mother is cared for. He makes sure the beloved disciple has someone to protect. Even in his final moments, he is binding people together, creating family where there is loss.

Saint Paul reminds us that this is what the body of Christ is always meant to do. We are not meant to be isolated parts, each perfect and complete on our own. We are a body, made whole only in connection with one another, each of us different, each of us necessary. The highest gift, Paul suggests, is not the most visible or dramatic one, but the one that builds up the whole. And the Psalmist sings: we are his people, the sheep of his flock, held together not by our own strength but by belonging to something larger than ourselves.

Mary stands beneath the cross, grieving. But she does not stand alone, and she is not left abandoned. A son is given to her. The disciple finds a mother. In that exchange, even in sorrow, there is the shape of the kingdom: people turning toward each other, making space for one another, saying yes to the work of becoming family.

You might sit quietly with the image of those standing near the cross. Who in your life has made space for you? For whom might you make space today?
